key_insight: Laser remelting densified detonation-sprayed NiCrFeBSiC coatings, increasing hardness and adhesion while reducing specific wear rate by 49.5%.
engineering_relevance: This combined coating process offers a promising route to wear-resistant protection for stainless-steel components in mechanical and power engineering.
method: Deposit NiCrFeBSiC onto AISI 321 stainless steel by detonation spraying, then laser remelt.
Compare microstructure and phases using SEM, EDS, and XRD.
Evaluate indentation properties, adhesion, friction, wear, and electrochemical corrosion.
evidence_signal: After remelting, porosity decreased from 0.306% to 0.15%, hardness increased from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV, and specific wear rate fell from 2.864 × 10⁻⁴ to 1.447 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m).
watch_item: Remelting reduced coating thickness, and the approximately 3% decrease in corrosion current density indicates only a modest corrosion benefit.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Remelting on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation-Sprayed NiCrFeBSiC Coatings for Mechanical Engineering Applications
